title: I Used the Moving-Truck Elevator Reservation Against the Board Member

parts.text: I reserved the freight elevator Saturday 8 to 12 with a forty-dollar hold. At 8:05 a board member, Frank, had a leather sofa stuck in the door and told my movers to wait. I was thirty, holding coffee and a clipboard the management office had stamped. Frank said board moves take priority. The policy binder said reservations take priority. My truck was eating street time. Then Frank's dog walker asked us to also hold the passenger elevator so the sofa would not scuff.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He wants both elevators and my paid window for a sofa that did not book.

social.video_title: The board sofa ate my paid freight window — Part 1/2
social.description: Forty-dollar hold, stamped clipboard, leather in the door. Then the passenger car. Would you have told the movers to push in?

parts.text: I called the management emergency line printed on the clipboard. They told Frank to clear freight. He did, complaining. I moved. The sofa waited for an open slot like furniture. The dog walker used the stairs. My hold was honored down to 11:58. Coffee went cold in a good cause. Board titles do not stamp clipboards. Reservations do.

social.video_title: The emergency line cleared the leather out of the door — Part 2/2
social.description: Window honored, sofa rescheduled, stairs for dogs. Was a title a reservation?
